misconceptions.description: Writing a policy that requires every student to use the AI tool, so learning stops when the tool, consent, or device is unavailable
misconceptions.trigger: memo mandates the tool with no equivalent non-AI path
misconceptions.feedback: Name a low-tech fallback that reaches the same learning target so no student's learning depends on the tool.

misconceptions.description: Leaving consent out of the memo so families who decline have no path and the AI tool becomes mandatory by default
misconceptions.trigger: memo is silent on opt-out and gives declining families no route
misconceptions.feedback: State the opt-out path. Families that decline still need an equivalent route to the same target.

misconceptions.description: Requiring AI tool use as homework, which penalizes students without reliable home devices or internet
misconceptions.trigger: memo assigns AI tool use outside school with no access note
misconceptions.feedback: Keep AI use in class on school devices, or provide an offline path, so home access is not a penalty.

misconceptions.description: Omitting whether the vendor retains student work for model training, leaving a privacy risk unaddressed
misconceptions.trigger: memo names no data-retention boundary for student text
misconceptions.feedback: State the privacy boundary: confirm student text is not retained by the vendor for training.
